chapter: With Chick Webb and Ella Fitzgerald, 1936-39
title: Playing Montgomery without knowing Webb had died
summary: The band played sets for a silent crowd until the manager told them Webb had died that afternoon.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Now when we get to the place -- Hampton, the beach, you know -- (inaudible) that night. Now,
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

we going on down Montgomery, Alabama. We get there. We play on an outside -- the guy got a great big -- he got a ballroom, but he also got an outside (inaudible) -- ballroom outside (inaudible). When we get there, five or six o'clock, it's getting dark, you know. (Inaudible) something to eat and we just cooling down (inaudible). When we get there, people are coming out like mad -- actually early. You don't see people coming to the dance this early, you know what I mean? And the place packs up. We get up on the bandstand -- the place packing up fast, you know. And I don't know who we had. We had Beeson on drums (inaudible). But the band was playing good, you know. The band was playing.
In other words, before Chick Webb died, Big Sid and sometimes Bill Beeson --
Bill Beeson. Big Sid Catlett made all the trips with us.
I see.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
But Bill Beeson was making this trip.
I see.
Because he was just going along to rest Chick up, see.
I see. So apparently, Sid wasn't available when Chick died.
No.
You might've taken him instead of Bill Beeson.

Might've been him. But anyway, about -- We played four sets. We played four good sets. And the funny thing, like all these sets that we played, we had like number one set, number two set, number three set -- and these were all like house rockers. If you know what I mean. This would upset any crowd. When we played the first set, didn't nobody clap or do nothing. Everybody just stood there and looked at us. The place was packed -- outside.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Everybody standing, milling around, people was coming in. We played another set, so Taft said, "What's wrong with these people out here? They don't like the band or something?"
So the road manager called Taft inside. He say, "Come here, I want to talk to you." He (Inaudible) went inside with the manager (inaudible). (Inaudible).
When he came back out, he told (inaudible), "You know that Chick Webb died today." Passed away this afternoon."
Now we didn't know that. We never knew that. We hadn't heard -- We were travelling all day long. We came straight off the road right into the ballroom -- right into the man's place.
He knew it. Everybody in town knew it. Everybody on the radio -- heard it all over the country. But the band didn't know it.
The band was the last to know.
We had played three sets.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
And the people hadn't even moved. People just milling around, (inaudible) their hands like that. I said, "Man, people don't like us there, you know. Maybe they don't like this band, you know."

We played another set (inaudible) singing (inaudible) carrying on. Some guy threw a bottle and almost hit (inaudible) Bobby. Almost hit him (inaudible), in the back, hit him on the shoulder (inaudible). Coca-cola bottle, you know.
We sitting up high, you know. Somebody threw a bottle, you know, hit him in his back (inaudible).
So then --
Where was this again?
Montgomery, Alabama.

So that little incident went down. So we played another set -- and after the third set, so he called us in. Told Taft, and (inaudible) he called the band. "We are going to take an (inaudible) intermission.
And he came out and announced it, "The dance is over." He cancelled it.
The band didn't know. The announcer (inaudible)
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
announced it and everything. People (inaudible). Cancelled the band out by eleven o'clock. We were getting ready to take intermission. We didn't go back up (inaudible). Everybody left.
Because we didn't -- the band didn't know that Chick had passed away. They was on the road and wasn't no way for them to find out, because they were travelling all day.
And that was right. We were travelling (inaudible). And we turned around and went right back to Baltimore.
